title: Video Editor for Instagram Reels
description:
We’re looking for a video editor who genuinely cares about the quality of the final product—not someone who rushes through edits just to get them done.



We want someone who understands why content performs: what makes someone stop scrolling, keep watching, and ultimately take action. Every cut, hook, sound, transition, and detail should have a purpose.



WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

- Takes pride in their work and pays attention to the small details

- Strong understanding of hooks, pacing, retention, and storytelling

- Knows how to edit content for performance, engagement, and conversions

- Can adapt to different creative styles: nostalgic, Y2K, raw footage, organic, etc.

- Willing to put in the extra effort to make an edit actually hit

- Can think independently instead of relying on step-by-step instructions

- Brings their own creative ideas and suggestions to the table

- Takes feedback well and improves with every revision

- Must be comfortable editing in CapCut



THE TYPE OF CONTENT

- TikTok / Reels-style short-form content

- Paid ads + organic content

- Product-focused storytelling

- Hook-driven, fast-paced, high-retention edits

- Nostalgic, raw, real-life aesthetics

- Content that feels native to social media—not overly polished or corporate



YOU’RE NOT A FIT IF YOU

- Rush edits just to deliver them quickly

- Throw clips together without thinking about the final result

- Don’t understand hooks, pacing, or viewer retention

- Need every detail explained before you can execute

- Use the same editing style for every piece of content

- Ignore small details

- Only execute instructions without contributing creatively



HOW TO APPLY — READ CAREFULLY

     1. Send us exactly 3 of your best TikTok-style edits. No more, no less.

     2. Upload the 3 edits to a Google Drive folder.

     3. Name the folder: Your Name / TOS Editor Position

     4. Make sure link access is enabled.

     5. Send us the Google Drive link.



Include a short note explaining how you approach an edit and what you focus on when trying to make content perform.

IMPORTANT: If you send a full portfolio, submit more than 3 edits, or don’t follow the instructions above, your application will be skipped.



LONG-TERM VISION

- We’re not looking for someone to complete a few edits and disappear.

- We want to find an editor we can build with long-term—someone who wants to grow alongside the brand and become an important part of the creative process.

- As the brand grows, we want your role to grow with it. That means more responsibility, more creative input, and more opportunities.

- We value people who constantly want to improve, experiment, and evolve their style. We want someone who can eventually understand our brand and content so well that they’re not just waiting for instructions—they’re bringing ideas to us.

- If you want a role where your creative decisions actually matter and where you can grow with what we’re building, we’d love to see your work.

title: Executive Virtual Assistant – U.S. Court Reporting Operations
description:
IMPORTANT: PLEASE READ BEFORE APPLYING



Before applying, please research what court reporting entails in the United States, including the basic transcript production process and the administrative work involved.



Previous Applicants Welcome! If you’ve applied to one of my earlier postings for this position, you’re absolutely welcome to apply again! I’ve updated the description to better reflect what I’m looking for. Please mention that you’re a returning applicant and complete the application questions below.



This is NOT a legal research, paralegal, or transcription position. You do not need to research laws, prepare legal documents, or transcribe proceedings.



A Little About Me & The Position



I own a U.S.-based court reporting business, Excel Reporting LLC, and I’m looking for someone who can become my right hand in managing the day-to-day administrative side of my business.



You’ll be working closely with me, side by side (remotely, of course!), so finding someone whose personality and working style are compatible with mine is important.



I’m friendly, approachable, and enjoy having fun while I work. I appreciate a good sense of humor, open communication, and a positive working relationship. That said, I take my business, commitments, and deadlines seriously, and I’m looking for someone who does too.



I want someone I can bounce ideas off of, who isn’t afraid to speak up, offer suggestions, or tell me when there’s a better way to do something. You don’t have to agree with me on everything! I actually appreciate someone who can respectfully challenge an idea and bring a different perspective.



I’m not looking for someone who simply waits for instructions or needs to be micromanaged. I want someone who takes initiative, anticipates needs, solves problems, and helps me find more efficient ways of doing things.



My goal is to build a comfortable, collaborative working relationship based on mutual respect, trust, accountability, and open communication.



Eventually, I’d love for you to take ownership of much of the administrative side of the business so I can focus on court reporting and transcript production.



What You’ll Be Helping Me With



* Scheduling & Calendaring: Managing my business calendar, coordinating assignments, monitoring availability, and preventing scheduling conflicts.

*
 Management: Organizing incoming
s, identifying urgent requests, drafting professional responses, and following up on outstanding matters.

* Transcript Production & Deadlines: Tracking assignments, strict turnaround deadlines, rush orders, production progress, and final deliveries.

* Billing & Invoicing: Preparing daily billing sheets, organizing billing information, tracking invoices, and monitoring outstanding payments.

* Vendor Coordination: Communicating with scopists, proofreaders, and court reporting agencies regarding assignments, deadlines, and outstanding work.

* Administrative Organization: Maintaining job trackers, attorney and contact databases, business expenses, and organized digital records.

* Business Operations: Monitoring renewals, recurring business payments, agency onboarding, and other administrative responsibilities.

* Process Improvement: Identifying inefficiencies, researching helpful tools, recommending better systems, and implementing improvements with approval.



You won’t be expected to know everything immediately. We’ll work together to establish systems and procedures, but I do expect you to be resourceful and willing to learn.



Communication Expectations



This is a written-communication-focused position. You will NOT be required to make phone calls or provide telephone-based customer service.



Most communication will take place through
, messaging platforms, and shared business tools.



Your accent or spoken English fluency is not a concern. What matters is your ability to read, comprehend, and write English at an advanced professional level.



You should be able to understand detailed written instructions, draft clear and professional
s, and communicate without unnecessary confusion.



Communication and accountability are extremely important to me.



If you’re overwhelmed, unsure about something, encounter a problem, make a mistake, or believe you may miss a deadline, I expect you to communicate that as soon as you become aware of it.



I would much rather know about a potential problem early so we can work through it together than discover it after a deadline has passed.



Who I’m Looking For



* Proactive & Independent: Takes initiative, anticipates needs, and follows through without constant reminders.

* Organized & Deadline-Conscious: Comfortable managing multiple priorities and strict deadlines.

* Excellent Written Communicator: Strong English reading comprehension, grammar, proofreading, and professional writing skills.

* Transparent & Accountable: Communicates concerns, mistakes, and potential delays promptly.

* Resourceful & Solutions-Oriented: Willing to research unfamiliar tasks and suggest solutions instead of immediately giving up.

* Improvement-Minded: Enjoys finding new tools, systems, and more efficient ways to work.

* Discreet & Trustworthy: Understands the importance of confidentiality and properly handling sensitive information.

* Confident & Collaborative: Comfortable asking questions, offering suggestions, and respectfully disagreeing when appropriate.

* Personable & Adaptable: Friendly, dependable, and comfortable working closely with a small-business owner.



Previous experience in U.S. court reporting operations, transcript production coordination, or similar administrative work is strongly preferred, but not required.



Strong executive assistant, scheduling,
 management, and administrative operations experience is also highly valued.



I care more about finding the right person than finding someone with a perfect resume.



Schedule & Flexibility



Starting Schedule: Approximately 10 hours per week, with potential for additional hours as the business grows.



During the initial onboarding and organization phase, there may be opportunities for additional hours while we establish systems, organize records, and streamline workflows.



I value work-life balance and flexibility.



You will not be expected to work more than four hours in a single day. If you’d like to work additional hours, we can discuss and mutually agree on that.



I’m also open to adjusting hours between days depending on workload, deadlines, and mutual availability. For example, a lighter day could be balanced by a busier day later in the week.



However, because court reporting is a deadline-driven industry, flexibility cannot interfere with urgent communications, scheduling requests, or transcript deadlines.



Some availability during U.S. Eastern business hours is necessary, and we’ll establish a reasonable schedule for checking time-sensitive matters.



Any additional hours must be agreed upon in advance and will be compensated.



Compensation



Negotiable based on experience and qualifications.



I’m looking for a long-term working relationship with opportunities for additional responsibilities and hours as the business grows.



Application Requirements – Please Answer ALL Questions



I’m hoping to find someone who has genuinely taken the time to understand the position rather than sending a generic application.



Please answer the following questions in your own words:



1. What does a court reporter do in the United States, and what is the basic transcript production process?

2. What is the difference between a court reporter, a scopist, and a proofreader?

3. If you’re managing several assignments and realize you may not meet an important deadline, how would you handle the situation, and when would you notify me?

4. Tell me about a time you independently identified an inefficient process or problem and recommended or implemented a better solution.

5. What kind of working relationship helps you do your best work, and how do you communicate with someone you work closely with?

6. What experience do you have with scheduling,
 management, billing, or administrative operations? How do you ensure confidential information remains protected?



Please also include your expected hourly rate, availability during U.S. Eastern business hours, and whether you’ve applied to one of my previous postings.



Applications that do not answer the questions will not be considered.



One Last Thing!



I’m genuinely excited to find the right person to work with!



I don’t expect perfection, and I don’t expect you to have all the answers. I do expect honesty, initiative, accountability, and a willingness to learn.



I’m kind, easy to communicate with, and happy to share what I know. I also appreciate someone who brings their own knowledge and ideas to the table.



I want this to feel like a team, not a situation where I’m constantly assigning tasks and checking behind someone.



If you’re dependable, resourceful, organized, and enjoy working closely with someone who’s friendly but serious about getting things done, I’d love to hear from you!

title: UGC Engineer
description:
About Chomp



Chomp is a free app where a little pet eats whatever you log, and your friends can see how you're doing. We grow through short videos on TikTok and Instagram, made by a team of creators we pay.



The role



You run our creator program from start to finish. Your job is to find out which messages, formats and creators reach the right people and get the app downloaded. Our current numbers show why: 0.3% of our videos get most of the views. So the work is to post a lot, spot the winners quickly, do more of what works and stop what doesn't.



This is not a "just edit videos" job. You own the results.



What you'll do



• Find trends: Spend time on TikTok and Reels every day. Spot formats, sounds and hooks that are taking off, and turn them into ideas our creators can film.

• Edit: Cut raw creator footage into short, punchy vertical videos (CapCut or similar), with strong hooks in the first 2 seconds.

• Post: Publish and schedule clips across our accounts. Write captions, choose hashtags and reply in comments.

• Find winners: Track views, saves, shares and comments every week. Report which hooks, formats and creators are working, and why.

• Manage creators: Onboard new creators, review what they submit, give clear feedback, run 1:1 coaching calls, and let go of creators who don't improve.

• Rewrite the brief weekly: Keep our creator brief current with the hooks, formats, reference videos and talking points that are working right now.

• Set up phones and accounts: Set up phones with proxies or SIMs so each account has its own clean identity. Create and warm up new TikTok and Instagram accounts until they're ready to post. Keep them healthy: no shadowbans, no flagged devices, no linked accounts. Help creators get their own accounts set up the same way.



You're a fit if you



• Spend hours on TikTok anyway and can explain why a video blew up

• Have edited short-form videos that got real views (show us)

• Have warmed up new TikTok accounts yourself and can explain your process step by step

• Have set up phones with mobile or residential proxies (or SIMs) and run several accounts without bans or shadowbans

• Write clear, direct English that creators act on

• Can give honest feedback and make hard calls about who stays

• Are comfortable with numbers and simple spreadsheets

• Have a reliable laptop, smartphone and internet with a backup



Bonus



• You've grown a TikTok account yourself (personal or for a brand)

• You've managed creators, an agency roster or a UGC team

• You know Gen Z and young millennial culture: cozy games, virtual pets, "girl dinner" content





How to apply



Send:



1. Links to 3–5 short-form videos you edited or posted, with view counts

2. One TikTok you saw this week that you think we should copy for Chomp. Tell us in 2–3 sentences how you'd adapt it

3. In 3–5 sentences, tell us how you'd warm up a brand-new TikTok account and set up its phone and proxy. Include how long you'd wait before the first post.

4. A short Loom or voice note (under 2 minutes) introducing yourself



Start your message with "Feed the pet" so we know you read this far. Applications without it won't be reviewed.
